sections.title: The Problem: Proximity vs. Privacy
lecture_lines: We must track exposure without identities.
Central servers should not track individuals.
animations: 1. Display proximity scenario (User A and User B) in white (#FFFFFF).
3. Highlight contact risk area in orange (#FFA500).
4. Display privacy concern text (red #FF0000) over user IDs.
5. Fade out all, ending with question mark in light blue (#00FFFF).

sections.title: Core Mechanism: Ephemeral Tracing Keys
lecture_lines: Phones generate secret Daily Tracing Keys.
animations: 1. Generate random daily key (color: #00FF00) for User A.
2. Derive ephemeral tracing keys (color: #FFFF00) from daily key.
3. Show keys rotating (animation: rotate) in sequence.

sections.title: The Exchange: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) Handshake
animations: 1. Show two devices exchanging encrypted packets (color: #FF00FF).
2. Visualize BLE signal strength as pulsing rings (#00FFFF).
3. Encrypt packet display using lock icon (color: #FFFFFF).

sections.title: Exposure Detection: The Decentralized Match
animations: 1. Central server publishes list of diagnosis keys (color: #FF0000).
2. Device downloads list, matches against stored contact keys.
3. Highlight positive match (color: #00FF00) on user device.

sections.title: Summary & Security Properties
animations: 2. Fade in checkmarks (color: #00FF00) next to properties.
3. Show summary text box (color: #FFFF00) highlighting privacy.
